claims.explanation: Nocodazole kills cells by disrupting microtubule polymerization, and the selective pattern is best explained by mitotic/checkpoint and microtubule-pathway context rather than by any single lineage. TP53 loss and other cell-cycle checkpoint defects (e.g., CDKN2A loss, FBXW7 mutation) sensitize cells because they cannot arrest properly after spindle damage, while intact p53 signaling and EGFR/MAPK-driven or slow-cycling contexts are protective. The strongest predictors are therefore damaging mutations in TP53/CDKN2A/FBXW7 and high expression of mitotic spindle/checkpoint genes.

features.basis: TP53 mutation is enriched in killed lines and loss of p53-mediated arrest after spindle damage increases nocodazole lethality
CDKN2A loss appears in killed lines and impairs cell-cycle checkpoint control
FBXW7 mutation is enriched among killed lines and can deregulate mitotic progression
Aurora B is required for spindle checkpoint signaling and nocodazole-arrested cells depend on it
Spindle assembly checkpoint activity determines response to microtubule disruption
Spindle assembly checkpoint activity determines response to microtubule disruption
Topoisomerase II is required at mitosis and its function interacts with nocodazole-induced spindle arrest
EGFR-mutant lung lines are overrepresented among least-affected lines
MAP2K1-mutant lung line is among least affected, suggesting MAPK-driven survival
KRAS-mutant lines are overrepresented among least-affected lines
PTEN mutation appears in several least-affected lines, possibly reflecting PI3K/AKT survival signaling
Dynein/dynactin-dependent microtubule functions are disrupted by nocodazole and affect mitotic and organelle transport
